pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: 1. Borrowings have nearly doubled and the earnings base has not caught up (Documentary Fact for the amounts, Analyst Interpretation for the reading). QXO, Inc.'s borrowings were USD 3,100.0 million at December 31, 2025 and March 31, 2026, USD 6,111 million at June 30, 2026 after USD 3,000 million of notes were sold into escrow for TopBuild, and USD 9,111 million after the USD 3,000 million incremental term loan on July 1, 2026. Reported gross leverage at June 30, 2026 was 8.43x and net leverage 4.60x, but the earnings measure of USD 724.8 million has no TopBuild contribution and only three months of Kodiak, while the debt includes the TopBuild financing. The mechanism is a timing mismatch between debt and earnings; the implication is that these ratios are not a steady-state reading and the third-quarter 2026 report is the next decisive evidence. [CP-1, CP-1A] 2. Adjusted EBITDA relies on large add-backs (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on recurrence). Of USD 724.8 million of last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA, USD 379.1 million (52.3%) is add-backs, including USD 127.5 million of stock compensation, USD 78.7 million of transaction costs, USD 68.9 million of transformation costs, USD 51.7 million of inventory fair value and USD 48.6 million of restructuring. EBITDA before the add-backs is USD 345.7 million, which gives gross leverage of 17.68x and net leverage of 9.65x at June 30, 2026. Restructuring, transaction and transformation items appear in each period reported, so QXO, Inc. may keep incurring them while it integrates three businesses; if they recur, leverage tolerance is weaker than the adjusted figures imply. [CP-1] 3. Interest cover is flattered by the timing of coupons (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation). Last-twelve-month cash interest was USD 221.0 million, giving cover of 3.28x, and cover was 2.58x in the six months to June 30, 2026. The coupons on the June 30, 2026 borrowings at printed rates are USD 401.0 million a year, so cover on that run-rate is about 1.81x before the incremental term loan, whose margin is not supplied, and before any TopBuild earnings. If the incremental loan were priced like the existing term loan, run-rate interest would be about USD 570.2 million and cover about 1.27x on earnings excluding TopBuild. This is an illustrative floor, not an estimate: it shows how much of the credit depends on TopBuild earnings. [CP-1] 4. Cash conversion is thin in the first half and after preferred dividends (Documentary Fact). Cash from operations was negative USD 146 million in the first half of 2026 as receivables and inventory built, and LTM cash from operations less capital expenditures was USD 141.2 million against preferred dividends paid of USD 143.8 million, leaving USD -2.6 million. The first quarter is seasonally weak and the company reports a net loss of USD 511.4 million over the period. [CP-1, CP-1A] 5. Liquidity and maturities are the main support (Documentary Fact). Liquidity was USD 4,704 million at June 30, 2026 (cash USD 2,774 million plus asset-based revolver availability USD 1,930 million), excluding USD 3,000 million of escrowed proceeds that funded the TopBuild closing. No scheduled principal on the June 30, 2026 borrowings falls due before the revolver's 2030 maturity (USD 11 million drawn); the maturities are USD 1,500 million in 2031, USD 3,100 million in 2032, USD 3,000 million in 2033 (the incremental loan) and USD 1,500 million in 2034. The springing fixed charge test on the revolver is not live, as availability of USD 1,930 million compares with a trigger of at most USD 200 million. The implication is low refinancing risk through 2030, but post-closing cash is Not supplied. [CP-1] 6. Rate exposure and claims ahead of or beside the debt are rising (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation). Floating-rate borrowings are 14.1% of June 30, 2026 borrowings and 42.4% including the incremental term loan, so 100 basis points adds about USD 38.6 million of annual interest. The USD 3,000 million of 2031 and 2034 notes are unsecured behind the secured revolver, term loans and 2032 notes, and the group has senior-to-common preferred stock whose dividends could reach USD 264.1 million a year. Series C holders can require cash redemption on a fundamental change, an event that also triggers a 101% put on the notes, and the amounts are not netted in any source. [CP-1, CP-1A] 7. Governance is documented but not fully assessable (Documentary Fact; Insufficient Information). Documented actions to date are a Kodiak purchase funded with preferred stock and shares, no common dividends and preferred dividends paid in cash, with an option to pay Series C dividends in shares. Voting power is concentrated in the chairman at about 22.1% and a 40% board designation right sits with his investor group, as of the annual report. Related-party arrangements, executed covenant definitions and current ownership percentages after the TopBuild share issuance are Not supplied. [CP-1A]

runs.text: Liquidity cushion (Documentary Fact). QXO, Inc. held USD 4,704 million of liquidity at June 30, 2026, against no scheduled principal on that debt until 2030, which gives it time to integrate before a refinancing wall. [CP-1]

Maturity and rate mix (Documentary Fact). 85.9% of June 30, 2026 borrowings were fixed-rate and the earliest large maturity is USD 1,500 million in 2031, which limits both refinancing and rate pressure until the incremental term loan lifts the floating share to 42.4%. [CP-1]

Customer and demand profile (Documentary Fact; Management Language on demand). No customer exceeded 1% of net sales and management describes repair and re-roofing demand as largely non-discretionary, which supports revenue visibility but is management characterisation, not audited fact. [CP-1A]

Equity-funded growth to date (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on cash retention). Kodiak was paid for with preferred stock and shares, with the target's own debt repaid at closing, and common dividends are not being paid, which retained cash inside the group. [CP-1A]

Covenant headroom (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation). The only described maintenance test is not live, with availability of USD 1,930 million against a trigger of at most USD 200 million, so covenant pressure is low until availability falls sharply. [CP-1]

Leverage unmeasured after closing (Insufficient Information). Borrowings of USD 9,111 million after the July 1, 2026 term loan have no matching reported earnings; the missing datapoints are TopBuild earnings and cash after closing, and they change every ratio. [CP-1, CP-1A]

Earnings quality (Analyst Interpretation). Add-backs make up 52.3% of Adjusted EBITDA, so management's adjusted figure depends on items that recur during integration. Last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA margin of 7.3% sits below the 9.5% reported for FY2025, although the FY2025 base holds Beacon only from April 29, 2025. [CP-1]

Cash flow after claims (Documentary Fact). Last-twelve-month cash from operations less capital expenditures of USD 141.2 million does not cover preferred dividends paid of USD 143.8 million, and the preferred burden can rise to USD 264.1 million a year. [CP-1, CP-1A]

Integration load (Analyst Interpretation). QXO, Inc. is integrating Beacon, Kodiak and TopBuild at once with TopBuild accounting incomplete, and management's plan to more than double EBITDA is management language that no filing figure yet confirms. [CP-1A]

Concentrations and control (Documentary Fact; Insufficient Information). Three suppliers made up nearly 35% of purchases, the business reports one operating segment so no segment profit is available, and control rights are concentrated; whether control is used against creditors is not evidenced either way. [CP-1A]

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Beacon (closed April 29, 2025). Under a merger agreement dated March 20, 2025, QXO acquired Beacon for a net purchase price that the June 2026 quarterly report gives as 10.64 billion (10-Q Q2 2026, page:53). Financing signed on April 29, 2025 comprised a 2.25 billion term loan, 2.25 billion of 6.75% senior secured notes due 2032 and an asset-based revolver of up to 2.0 billion, alongside equity raised in 2024 and 2025; the pages read do not give a full sources and uses table. A voluntary 1.40 billion term loan prepayment followed on May 29, 2025, and the quarterly report states that the equity proceeds of May 2025 were used to repay term loan debt (10-Q Q2 2026, page:21 and page:48). The term loan margin was reduced in November 2025. Beacon is treated as the predecessor for financial reporting (10-K, page:67).

Kodiak (closed April 1, 2026). QXO agreed on February 10, 2026 to buy Kodiak from Court Square Capital Partners and closed on April 1, 2026 for a net purchase price of 2.22 billion according to the quarterly report; the annual report's earlier figure was approximately 2.25 billion and the share count is stated as 13.2 million and 13.3 million in different places (logged in conflicts below, not reconciled). Consideration was cash of 478 to sellers, 1,503 to settle Kodiak's secured term loan and asset-based facility including accrued interest, and 257 of QXO shares. Series C proceeds funded a portion of the cash: 200,000 shares of Series C Preferred Stock were issued for 2.0 billion gross proceeds to funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management, Inc. Kodiak added net sales of 595 and net income of 15 in the second quarter of 2026. Status: complete, with purchase accounting preliminary.

TopBuild (closed July 1, 2026, a subsequent event for the June 30, 2026 balance sheet). The merger agreement dated April 18, 2026 values the deal at approximately 15 billion in cash and stock. About 91.0% of TopBuild holders elected cash, and after proration each TopBuild share received about 249.67 in cash and 10.212 QXO shares; QXO issued about 312.0 million shares and paid about 6.4 billion in cash. Use of proceeds named in the filing: 3.0 billion of senior notes (6.500% due July 15, 2031 and 6.875% due July 15, 2034) sold on June 17, 2026 into a segregated escrow and released on closing; a 3.0 billion incremental term loan under the existing term loan agreement maturing July 1, 2033; and 1.0 billion from the remaining 100,000 shares of Series C Preferred Stock, which exhausted the 3.0 billion Series C commitment. The filing says the initial accounting is incomplete and that preliminary purchase price allocation is expected in the quarterly report for the period ending September 30, 2026. It does not say whether TopBuild's own debt was assumed or repaid, what cash TopBuild brought, or the cash left after closing; these are Insufficient Information and matter directly for liquidity and leverage.

New debt issues, summarised for the creditor. The 2031 and 2034 notes are guaranteed by the subsidiaries that guarantee the term loan and the 2032 notes and are unsecured after the escrow release, so they rank behind the secured term loan, secured notes and asset-based revolver on the collateral; each carries a 101% put on specified change of control and, for these two series, ratings events. The incremental term loan is floating rate with a margin not stated in the pages read, 1% annual amortisation and a 1.00% repricing premium for six months. Preferred stock raised alongside the debt adds senior-to-common claims at the parent. Quantities are in the financial base handoff. Liquidity effect: the 3,000 of escrow cash was excluded from liquidity of 4,704 at June 30, 2026 and was spent on closing, so the post-closing liquidity position is Not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - **Subsequent event is incomplete.** The TopBuild closing date is after the balance sheet date, and the filing says: page:26: "initial accounting for the business combination is incomplete and the Company is not yet able to disclose the provisional amounts". Mechanism: the June 30 balance sheet shows escrowed proceeds as restricted cash, page:8 of the August release footnote: "restricted cash of $3.0 billion, representing the gross proceeds from the issuance of the 6.500% Senior Notes due 2031 and 6.875% Senior Notes due 2034". Debt, preferred stock, shares and earnings capacity after July 1, 2026 therefore sit outside the reported balance sheet. Consequence: any leverage or liquidity measure built on June 30, 2026 figures mixes a pre-closing balance sheet with a financing that closed on July 1, 2026, and downstream modules must show a pro forma debt bridge from narrative only and label it as constructed.

fields.name: Quote

Beacon was determined the predecessor (page:12). The pack carries no complete Beacon predecessor statements: page:98: "The predecessor financial information is included as Exhibit 99.1 to this Quarterly Report and is incorporated herein by reference" and the exhibit index (page:99) shows it as a prior filing, not in the pack. Consequence: FY2025 and first-half 2025 comparatives are not like-for-like with 2026, and Kodiak contributes only from April 1, 2026 (August release page:1: "from the date of acquisition on April 1, 2026"). Trailing twelve-month figures would blend four different perimeters.

Conflict locators: May release page:1 "$ 1,730.2" versus August release page:1 "$ 4,976". Consequence: sums across periods can differ by rounding; this is a presentation difference, not a restatement, and no restatement was found by a search for restatement language beyond the cover check box.

Consequence: covenant definitions, baskets, restricted payment tests, guarantor lists and change-of-control terms are known only through the note summaries. The filing says restrictions are not significant for common dividends (page:51), which is a management statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The reported base supports a clear picture through June 30, 2026 and a bounded one after it. Through March 31, 2026 the group had 3,100.0 of borrowings (a term loan and secured notes), no drawing on its asset-based revolver, and cash almost equal to borrowings, so net debt was small. During the second quarter it bought Kodiak with preferred equity and shares, and in June it sold 3,000 of new notes whose proceeds sat in escrow until TopBuild closed on July 1, 2026. The June 30 balance sheet therefore shows borrowings of 6,111 but also 3,000 of restricted cash that is not counted in liquidity. After closing there are a further 3,000 incremental term loan and 1,000 of Series C preferred stock, which are reported only as subsequent events. Earnings are measured on company-defined Adjusted EBITDA, which excludes TopBuild, includes Kodiak only from April 1, 2026, and adds back stock compensation, restructuring, transaction, transformation and inventory fair value items. Seasonality is strong: the first quarter earns almost nothing and the half-year cash flow from operations is negative. Every ratio below is therefore labelled with its perimeter and is not a pro forma figure.

fields.value: 6. Pro forma borrowings at July 1, 2026 = 6,111 + incremental term loan 3,000 = 9,111. The 3,000 of notes released from escrow are already inside 6,111. Contractual coupon run-rate on June 30, 2026 borrowings at printed rates = 850 x 5.64% + 2,250 x 6.75% + 1,500 x 6.500% + 1,500 x 6.875% + 11 x 4.70% = 47.9 + 151.9 + 97.5 + 103.1 + 0.5 = 401.0 (rounded components sum to 400.9), before the incremental term loan whose margin is not supplied. If the stated June 2026 figure were instead before letters of credit, liquidity would be 4,642.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit story is an acquisition-led roll-up. QXO changed from a small software business into a roofing distributor on April 29, 2025 by buying Beacon, added Kodiak (lumber, trusses, windows and doors, construction supplies) on April 1, 2026, and agreed on April 18, 2026 to buy TopBuild (insulation distribution and installation), which closed on July 1, 2026, after the latest balance sheet date. The operating business is a branch-based distributor with a diversified customer base, no customer above 1% of sales, concentrated suppliers, strong seasonality and results driven by repair and re-roofing demand that management describes as largely non-discretionary. Each deal was paid for with a different mix: Kodiak with preferred stock and shares while its own debt was repaid, TopBuild with new debt, preferred stock and shares. Debt sits at the operating subsidiary; preferred stock, which carries senior-to-common cash dividends and a cash redemption right on a fundamental change for the Series C holders, sits at the parent. For a creditor the questions are integration execution on three businesses at once, how much of the added earnings reach the borrower's cash flow, and how control rights and preferred claims are used. The sources describe actions to date but not the executed covenant packages or any related-party arrangements, so governance conclusions are bounded.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Beacon (closed April 29, 2025). Under a merger agreement dated March 20, 2025, QXO acquired Beacon for a net purchase price that the June 2026 quarterly report gives as 10.64 billion (10-Q Q2 2026, page:53). Financing signed on April 29, 2025 comprised a 2.25 billion term loan, 2.25 billion of 6.75% senior secured notes due 2032 and an asset-based revolver of up to 2.0 billion, alongside equity raised in 2024 and 2025; the pages read do not give a full sources and uses table. A voluntary 1.40 billion term loan prepayment followed on May 29, 2025, and the quarterly report states that the equity proceeds of May 2025 were used to repay term loan debt (10-Q Q2 2026, page:21 and page:48). The term loan margin was reduced in November 2025. Beacon is treated as the predecessor for financial reporting (10-K, page:67).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Kodiak (closed April 1, 2026). QXO agreed on February 10, 2026 to buy Kodiak from Court Square Capital Partners and closed on April 1, 2026 for a net purchase price of 2.22 billion according to the quarterly report; the annual report's earlier figure was approximately 2.25 billion and the share count is stated as 13.2 million and 13.3 million in different places (logged in conflicts below, not reconciled). Consideration was cash of 478 to sellers, 1,503 to settle Kodiak's secured term loan and asset-based facility including accrued interest, and 257 of QXO shares. Series C proceeds funded a portion of the cash: 200,000 shares of Series C Preferred Stock were issued for 2.0 billion gross proceeds to funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management, Inc. Kodiak added net sales of 595 and net income of 15 in the second quarter of 2026. Status: complete, with purchase accounting preliminary.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: TopBuild (closed July 1, 2026, a subsequent event for the June 30, 2026 balance sheet). The merger agreement dated April 18, 2026 values the deal at approximately 15 billion in cash and stock. About 91.0% of TopBuild holders elected cash, and after proration each TopBuild share received about 249.67 in cash and 10.212 QXO shares; QXO issued about 312.0 million shares and paid about 6.4 billion in cash. Use of proceeds named in the filing: 3.0 billion of senior notes (6.500% due July 15, 2031 and 6.875% due July 15, 2034) sold on June 17, 2026 into a segregated escrow and released on closing; a 3.0 billion incremental term loan under the existing term loan agreement maturing July 1, 2033; and 1.0 billion from the remaining 100,000 shares of Series C Preferred Stock, which exhausted the 3.0 billion Series C commitment. The filing says the initial accounting is incomplete and that preliminary purchase price allocation is expected in the quarterly report for the period ending September 30, 2026. It does not say whether TopBuild's own debt was assumed or repaid, what cash TopBuild brought, or the cash left after closing; these are Insufficient Information and matter directly for liquidity and leverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt issues, summarised for the creditor. The 2031 and 2034 notes are guaranteed by the subsidiaries that guarantee the term loan and the 2032 notes and are unsecured after the escrow release, so they rank behind the secured term loan, secured notes and asset-based revolver on the collateral; each carries a 101% put on specified change of control and, for these two series, ratings events. The incremental term loan is floating rate with a margin not stated in the pages read, 1% annual amortisation and a 1.00% repricing premium for six months. Preferred stock raised alongside the debt adds senior-to-common claims at the parent. Quantities are in the financial base handoff. Liquidity effect: the 3,000 of escrow cash was excluded from liquidity of 4,704 at June 30, 2026 and was spent on closing, so the post-closing liquidity position is Not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. Acquisition-led growth. Evidence: three acquisitions in about fourteen months and 6,111 of borrowings at June 30, 2026 before a further 3,000 incremental term loan (from the financial base). Risk mechanic: earnings from Kodiak and TopBuild must replace the cash flow burdened by new interest, preferred dividends and integration and transaction costs; first-half 2026 operating cash flow was negative and trailing Adjusted EBITDA excludes TopBuild. Credit implication: leverage tolerance and debt service depend on integration delivery that is not yet visible in reported figures; monitoring posture should treat the third-quarter 2026 report as the next decisive evidence. Countering evidence: liquidity of 4,704 before closing and no scheduled principal on the June 30, 2026 debt before 2030.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Revenue durability. Evidence: no customer above 1% of sales, repair and re-roofing share described by management as non-discretionary, 97% U.S. sales. Mechanic: demand tied to weather and the housing stock, but first-quarter earnings are near nil, so cash timing is seasonal. Implication: revenue is durable at the customer level; working capital and liquidity must carry the first quarter. Countering: supplier concentration of nearly 35% in three suppliers and vendor rebate dependence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Margin and cash flow. Evidence: product cost increases outpaced selling price increases in 2026, and the company adds back large restructuring, transaction and transformation costs (financial base). Mechanic: incomplete pass-through of product costs compresses gross margin. Implication: cash conversion and the quality of Adjusted EBITDA are the key uncertainties, not top-line growth.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Claims ahead of and beside debt. Evidence: Series C holders can require cash redemption at the greater of stated value plus accrued dividends and as-converted value on a fundamental change, alongside the 101% put on the notes. Mechanic: a change of control triggers both a debt put and a preferred cash call on the same event. Implication: the preferred cash call and the notes put arise from the same event and the amounts are not netted in any source; the Series C stated value of 3,000 compares with liquidity of 4,704 before closing (see Calculations). This is a mechanic, not a recovery view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. Control and alignment. Evidence: voting concentration and board designation rights. Mechanic: control rights can influence capital allocation and approval of extraordinary transactions. Implication: willingness cannot be inferred from ownership identity; the documented behaviour to date is equity-funded growth and no common dividends, which is supportive, but the absence of executed covenant documents leaves capacity unassessed. Countering: none logged.

All amounts in prose below are USD millions unless a ratio or percentage is shown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: QXO, Inc. is a liquid but heavily acquisitive credit whose leverage cannot yet be measured on the enlarged group, so the fundamental view is cautious and conditional on integration. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 4,704 million at June 30, 2026, no scheduled principal on that debt before 2030 and a customer base with no customer above 1% of sales. The weakest point is that borrowings of USD 6,111 million, rising to USD 9,111 million after the July 1, 2026 term loan, are measured against last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 724.8 million that excludes TopBuild, 52.3% of which comes from add-backs. What decides the outcome is whether TopBuild and Kodiak earnings arrive and whether the add-backs fade. [CP-1, CP-1A]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Thesis (Analyst Interpretation): QXO, Inc. has funded a roll-up of three businesses with a mix of preferred equity, shares and USD 9,111 million of borrowings, and its credit quality is set by whether the enlarged group converts that scale into cash earnings that comfortably exceed its interest and preferred dividend burden. [CP-1, CP-1A]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. Borrowings have nearly doubled and the earnings base has not caught up (Documentary Fact for the amounts, Analyst Interpretation for the reading). QXO, Inc.'s borrowings were USD 3,100.0 million at December 31, 2025 and March 31, 2026, USD 6,111 million at June 30, 2026 after USD 3,000 million of notes were sold into escrow for TopBuild, and USD 9,111 million after the USD 3,000 million incremental term loan on July 1, 2026. Reported gross leverage at June 30, 2026 was 8.43x and net leverage 4.60x, but the earnings measure of USD 724.8 million has no TopBuild contribution and only three months of Kodiak, while the debt includes the TopBuild financing. The mechanism is a timing mismatch between debt and earnings; the implication is that these ratios are not a steady-state reading and the third-quarter 2026 report is the next decisive evidence. [CP-1, CP-1A]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Adjusted EBITDA relies on large add-backs (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on recurrence). Of USD 724.8 million of last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA, USD 379.1 million (52.3%) is add-backs, including USD 127.5 million of stock compensation, USD 78.7 million of transaction costs, USD 68.9 million of transformation costs, USD 51.7 million of inventory fair value and USD 48.6 million of restructuring. EBITDA before the add-backs is USD 345.7 million, which gives gross leverage of 17.68x and net leverage of 9.65x at June 30, 2026. Restructuring, transaction and transformation items appear in each period reported, so QXO, Inc. may keep incurring them while it integrates three businesses; if they recur, leverage tolerance is weaker than the adjusted figures imply. [CP-1]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Interest cover is flattered by the timing of coupons (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation). Last-twelve-month cash interest was USD 221.0 million, giving cover of 3.28x, and cover was 2.58x in the six months to June 30, 2026. The coupons on the June 30, 2026 borrowings at printed rates are USD 401.0 million a year, so cover on that run-rate is about 1.81x before the incremental term loan, whose margin is not supplied, and before any TopBuild earnings. If the incremental loan were priced like the existing term loan, run-rate interest would be about USD 570.2 million and cover about 1.27x on earnings excluding TopBuild. This is an illustrative floor, not an estimate: it shows how much of the credit depends on TopBuild earnings. [CP-1]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Cash conversion is thin in the first half and after preferred dividends (Documentary Fact). Cash from operations was negative USD 146 million in the first half of 2026 as receivables and inventory built, and LTM cash from operations less capital expenditures was USD 141.2 million against preferred dividends paid of USD 143.8 million, leaving USD -2.6 million. The first quarter is seasonally weak and the company reports a net loss of USD 511.4 million over the period. [CP-1, CP-1A]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. Liquidity and maturities are the main support (Documentary Fact). Liquidity was USD 4,704 million at June 30, 2026 (cash USD 2,774 million plus asset-based revolver availability USD 1,930 million), excluding USD 3,000 million of escrowed proceeds that funded the TopBuild closing. No scheduled principal on the June 30, 2026 borrowings falls due before the revolver's 2030 maturity (USD 11 million drawn); the maturities are USD 1,500 million in 2031, USD 3,100 million in 2032, USD 3,000 million in 2033 (the incremental loan) and USD 1,500 million in 2034. The springing fixed charge test on the revolver is not live, as availability of USD 1,930 million compares with a trigger of at most USD 200 million. The implication is low refinancing risk through 2030, but post-closing cash is Not supplied. [CP-1]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 6. Rate exposure and claims ahead of or beside the debt are rising (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation). Floating-rate borrowings are 14.1% of June 30, 2026 borrowings and 42.4% including the incremental term loan, so 100 basis points adds about USD 38.6 million of annual interest. The USD 3,000 million of 2031 and 2034 notes are unsecured behind the secured revolver, term loans and 2032 notes, and the group has senior-to-common preferred stock whose dividends could reach USD 264.1 million a year. Series C holders can require cash redemption on a fundamental change, an event that also triggers a 101% put on the notes, and the amounts are not netted in any source. [CP-1, CP-1A]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 7. Governance is documented but not fully assessable (Documentary Fact; Insufficient Information). Documented actions to date are a Kodiak purchase funded with preferred stock and shares, no common dividends and preferred dividends paid in cash, with an option to pay Series C dividends in shares. Voting power is concentrated in the chairman at about 22.1% and a 40% board designation right sits with his investor group, as of the annual report. Related-party arrangements, executed covenant definitions and current ownership percentages after the TopBuild share issuance are Not supplied. [CP-1A]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity cushion (Documentary Fact). QXO, Inc. held USD 4,704 million of liquidity at June 30, 2026, against no scheduled principal on that debt until 2030, which gives it time to integrate before a refinancing wall. [CP-1]

[CP-1A]
